text:
The tragedy-sniffers are
everywhere
they get up in the morning
and start finding things
wrong.

And they plunge
into rage,
a rage that lasts until
they go to bed,
and even there
they writhe in their
insomnia,
unable to remove
from their minds
the small obstacles
they have found.

They feel opposed,
it is a conspiracy.

And because they are constantly
furious they feel that
they are always
right.

You see them in traffic
honking like savages
at the slightest infraction,
cursing,
scattering their
insults.

You feel them
in bank lines,
in supermarkets,
in cinemas
pressing
against your back
treading on your heels
impatient for
a fury.

They are everywhere
and in
everything,
those souls
violently
unhappy.

In truth they are frightened,
as always they want to
be right
whipping
without cease…
it is an evil
a disease of
that race.

The first of them
I saw was
my father
and since then
I have seen a thousand fathers
wasting their lives
in hatred,
throwing their lives
into the blind well
and screaming
like madmen.

translation.title: They Are Everywhere
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The mixed regional forms and harsh repetitive cadence are rendered in direct English.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
